name: Social anarchism
summary: Social anarchism is the collectivist, left-wing branch of anarchism. It holds that liberty and solidarity go together, and that the state and capitalism are linked hierarchies to be replaced by common ownership and a bottom-up federation of free associations built on mutual aid. It favours direct action, direct decision-making and means that match its ends, and rejects parties, vanguards and the market.
scope: Social anarchism: the collectivist, class-struggle and revolutionary branch of anarchism, which Morland (s6) calls the classical anarchism of Bakunin and Kropotkin and which the FARJ (s7) defines as the anarchism of social transformation, in the line of Bakunin, Kropotkin and Malatesta and in Bookchin's dichotomy with lifestyle anarchism (s5). The Stanford Encyclopedia (s2) places it with anarchist communism and communitarian anarchism. Excludes individualist anarchism, anarcho-capitalism, lifestyle anarchism, primitivism and Marxist state socialism; mutualists and collectivists differ on wages and markets.
